stories.title: For U.S. Life Sciences Real Estate, 2026 Is a Tale of Stabilization
stories.excerpt: The U.S. life sciences real estate market remains oversupplied, but improving funding conditions and a sharply reduced construction pipeline are beginning to set the stage for a recovery, according to Cushman & Wakefield. Asking rents at U.S. life sciences facilities averaged $64.17 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, down 5.3 percent compared to last year, and vacancy climbed nearly 200 basis points to 24.3 percent. Cushman & Wakefield expects market rents to continue to slip, particularly in heavily supplied regions, but said stronger funding and occupier demand could stabilize rates over the next 18 to 24 months. Life sciences inventory has expanded from 171 million square feet in 2021 to 239 million square feet today, but the construction pipeline now represents only 2 percent of inventory, down from 17 percent at its mid-2023 peak. Just 1.2 million square feet was delivered through the first half of this year, which is an 82 percent decline from the first half of 2025, with future development increasingly concentrated in pre-leased and build-to-suit projects. Capital markets are also gradually reopening. R&D investment sales totaled more than $9.3 billion during the four quarters ending in June, up 4 percent from a year earlier. Deal count rose 9 percent to 292, above the prior 10-year average, although average transaction size declined 5 percent. Globally, venture capital investment reached $29.9 billion in the first half of 2026, up 30 percent from last year, and the strongest first-half showing since 2022. North America accounted for $17.9 billion, up 35 percent. IPO volume nearly tripled to $6.8 billion, while global mergers and acquisitions activity reached $97.2 billion, nearly three times its level a year earlier. San Diego County remains one of North America’s largest life sciences hubs, with 26.6 million square feet of inventory and asking rents averaging $67.09 per square foot. bullets: Life sciences asking rents fell 5.3% YoY to $64.17/sf; vacancy climbed 200 bps to 24.3%.
Construction pipeline shrunk to 2% of inventory; inventory expanded 171M to 239M sf since 2021.
Improved funding conditions and reduced pipeline expected to stabilize rents over 18–24 months.
stories.summary: U.S. life sciences real estate remains oversupplied with Q2 2026 asking rents down 5.3% year-over-year to $64.17/sf and vacancy at 24.3%, but Cushman & Wakefield expects stabilization within 18–24 months. Inventory has ballooned from 171M sf in 2021 to 239M sf today, though the construction pipeline has collapsed to just 2% of total inventory, down from higher levels. Stronger funding conditions and occupier demand should eventually support rent recovery, particularly as supply constraints tighten.
stories.impact: Life sciences development is temporarily constrained across most U.S. markets, but the sharp pipeline contraction signals a near-term window for selective new supply. Developers should monitor funding environments and occupier demand signals closely; markets with below-average vacancy (e.g., Boston, San Francisco) and lower future delivery may emerge as acquisition and development targets before broader sector recovery occurs.

stories.title: Berkadia Adds Experienced Multifamily Sales Team in Boston
stories.excerpt: Berkadia has added senior managing Directors Kevin Gleason and Brendan Shields and director Maggie McFarland to its investment sales platform in Boston. Gleason, Shields and McFarland specialize in multifamily investment sales and capitalizations across the New England region. With more than 40 years of combined experience in commercial real estate, they have successfully completed more than $15 billion in volume across property sales and capitalizations. Gleason, Shields, and McFarland bring extensive expertise in multifamily investment sales, strong client relationships and an extensive track record across the New England region, according to Berkadia. The new team will collaborate closely with the firm’s mortgage banking partners in the region to form a well-rounded, client-focused team. Before joining Berkadia, Gleason, Shields and McFarland were part of Walker & Dunlop’s investment sales platform in Boston. Prior to that, the team spent five years within the Capital Markets Group at JLL. The post Berkadia Adds Experienced Multifamily Sales Team in Boston appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Berkadia hired 3 senior brokers from W&D Boston with $15B combined multifamily sales volume.
Team specializes in New England multifamily investment sales and capitalizations.
Move signals increased capital markets activity and lender competition in Boston multifamily.
stories.summary: Berkadia added Kevin Gleason, Brendan Shields, and Maggie McFarland—three senior investment sales directors with 40+ years combined experience and $15 billion in transaction volume—to its Boston multifamily platform. The hires follow their tenure at Walker & Dunlop's investment sales team and JLL's Capital Markets Group. Berkadia positioned the team to collaborate with mortgage banking partners to strengthen its regional market position.
stories.impact: Increased broker hiring and platform expansion in Boston signal robust transactional activity and competition for deal flow in the region's multifamily market. This suggests strong pricing, capital availability, and portfolio churn in the metro, indicating a healthy environment for acquisitions and refinancings but potentially tighter bid-ask spreads for sellers.

stories.title: AI Startup Thinking Machines Lab Takes 22K SF at 79 Fifth Avenue for First NYC Office
stories.excerpt: Artificial intelligence research startup Thinking Machines Lab is coming to New York. Just a year and a half after launching in San Francisco, the company has inked a 21,500-square-foot lease at Kalimian Properties’ 79 Fifth Avenue just one block west of Union Square, Commercial Observer has learned. The terms of the deal were not disclosed, but asking rents in the 18-story office building hover slightly above $100 per square foot, according to a source familiar with the deal. Thinking Machines Lab was founded in early 2025 by Mira Murati, former chief technology officer at OpenAI, to design specialized AI models and create tools for researchers and businesses to train their own models. The company achieved a $12 billion valuation in July 2025. JLL’s Justin Haber and Kyle Riker negotiated the lease on behalf of the tenant, while Newmark’s David Falk, Daniel Levine and Dylan Weisman represented the landlord. A spokesperson for JLL confirmed the lease but declined to comment on the deal. The team at Newmark did not respond to a request for comment. Thinking Machines Lab’s new East Coast home will occupy the entire fourth floor of 79 Fifth Avenue. The building between East 15th and East 16th streets is also home to consulting company Capgemini America, streaming giant Hulu, and The New School. It is also home to fashion retailer Free People on the ground floor. Kalimian Properties’ Albert Kalimian did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the deal. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Thinking Machines Lab (ex-OpenAI CTO) leased 21.5K sf at 79 Fifth Avenue, Union Square area.
Startup valued at $12B in July 2025; asking rents ~$100/sf; 1.5-year-old San Francisco firm.
AI research growth driving office demand in Manhattan's prime tech corridor.
stories.summary: Thinking Machines Lab, a $12 billion AI research startup founded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, signed a 21,500-sf lease at 79 Fifth Avenue near Union Square at asking rents slightly above $100/sf. The company, launched in early 2025 in San Francisco, is establishing its first NYC office as it scales. JLL negotiated on behalf of the tenant; Newmark represented the landlord.
stories.impact: High-growth AI startups and research labs are anchoring Manhattan office demand in prime submarkets like Union Square and Flatiron, signaling sustained tenant interest despite broader office headwinds. This reinforces that trophy office locations and specialized research/tech clusters will command premium rents and drive selective multifamily demand from both employees and relocating talent in Manhattan and nearby Brooklyn/Queens submarkets.

stories.title: JV Acquires Value-Add Escondido Multifamily
stories.excerpt: Institutional Property Advisors (IPA), a division of Marcus & Millichap serving the company’s institutional clients, closed the sale of Pacifica Palms Apartments, a 189-unit multifamily property in Escondido. The purchase price was $33.6 million. “The Escondido submarket has seen limited availability of multifamily assets of this size, making Pacifica Palms a rare, large value-add investment opportunity in a supply-constrained market,” said Chris Zorbas, IPA executive managing director. Zorbas and IPA executive managing director Alexander Garcia, Jr., represented the seller, Pacifica Palms LLC, and procured the buyer, a joint venture between Stratford Partners and LLJ. “Escondido continues to grow and home prices have increased 19% since 2021,” said Garcia. “The disparity between monthly living expenses for renting vs. owning should sustain low vacancy and place upward pressure on Escondido’s rental prices for the foreseeable future.” Built in 1965, Pacifica Palms Apartments is a gated-entry, 20-building property with a children’s playground and picnic park, laundry facilities and open parking spaces. The post JV Acquires Value-Add Escondido Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Stratford Partners & LLJ JV acquired 189-unit Pacifica Palms, Escondido, for $33.6M.
Property built 1965, gated, value-add opportunity in supply-constrained market.
Home prices up 19% since 2021; rent-vs-own disparity supports low vacancy and rental growth.
stories.summary: A joint venture between Stratford Partners and LLJ closed on Pacifica Palms Apartments, a 189-unit value-add property in Escondido, California, for $33.6 million. Built in 1965, the gated community offers 20 buildings with amenities including a playground, laundry, and parking. IPA/Marcus & Millichap noted limited multifamily asset availability in the submarket, with home prices up 19% since 2021, supporting strong rental demand.
stories.impact: Escondido's constrained multifamily supply and rising home prices (19% appreciation since 2021) create a favorable rent growth environment and value-add opportunity window. Developers should monitor San Diego County inland submarkets for acquisition and redevelopment prospects, as the rent-vs.-own arbitrage widens and employment growth continues in the region.

stories.title: Northwest Bank to Open 75K-SF Corporate Headquarters in Ohio
stories.excerpt: Northwest Bank plans to open its new corporate headquarters in Dublin, Ohio, located in Bridge North, a new mixed-use development by the Daimler Group in the city’s Bridge Street District. The mixed-use development will include office, hospitality, retail and public gathering spaces. In addition to the Daimler Group, Northwest Bank is partnering with local architectural firm Moody Nolan for the space design and JLL for brokerage and project management services. The company anticipates moving its current headquarters in Easton to a new 75,000-square-foot building in the first half of 2029. The purpose-built space is designed to accommodate Northwest Bank’s headquarters workforce, which is expected to more than double by 2034, and its initial lease term is 15 years. “This investment represents an important step in Northwest Bank’s continued growth and transformation,” said Louis J. Torchio, president and chief executive officer of Northwest Bank. “Dublin’s collaborative approach to supporting businesses makes it an ideal location for Northwest Bank’s future headquarters.” The post Northwest Bank to Open 75K-SF Corporate Headquarters in Ohio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Northwest Bank relocating HQ to Dublin, Ohio; 75K sf purpose-built office; expected move H1 2029.
Workforce expected to more than double by 2034; 15-year initial lease term.
Bridge North mixed-use development by Daimler Group; Dublin's business-friendly environment cited.
stories.summary: Northwest Bank plans to relocate its corporate headquarters from Easton to a new 75,000-sf purpose-built office in Dublin, Ohio's Bridge North mixed-use development (developed by Daimler Group) in the Bridge Street District. The company expects to occupy the space in H1 2029 and projects its headquarters workforce will more than double by 2034, with a 15-year initial lease term. JLL is providing brokerage and project management services.
stories.impact: Northwest Bank's planned workforce doubling by 2034 signals significant job creation and population inflow to the Dublin/Columbus metro, driving multifamily demand growth over the next 5–10 years. Developers should assess land and site acquisition opportunities in Dublin and surrounding submarkets to capture the influx of bank employees and ancillary service workers; the announcement provides a concrete anchor for long-term population and housing demand modeling.

stories.title: Jadian Capital Secures $277M Apollo Loan for 37-Property IOS Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Jadian Capital, a New York City and Stamford, CT-based investment firm focused on alternative real estate and asset-intensive businesses, said Wednesday that JIOS, its vertically integrated industrial outdoor storage (IOS) platform, has secured a $277-million loan from affiliates of Apollo Global Management for a 37-property IOS portfolio spanning 23 markets. ”JIOS has now secured over $800 million of debt in 2026 to fuel the growth of our national portfolio,” said Dan Schuchinsky, managing director at Jadian. “This financing demonstrates the continued growth of institutional lender interest in IOS and we’re pleased to add Apollo to our capital provider relationships.” The portfolio is concentrated in infill locations near key logistics hubs and dense population nodes with a diverse tenant base spanning equipment rental, building materials, logistics and home services. With the support of Jadian, JIOS owns or controls more than 225 assets representing approximately $2.2 billion in value across 30-plus markets. Pictured: A JIOS property at 651 Fountain Ave. in Brooklyn. The post Jadian Capital Secures $277M Apollo Loan for 37-Property IOS Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Jadian Capital's JIOS secured $277M Apollo loan for 37-property industrial outdoor storage portfolio.
Portfolio spans 23 markets, concentrated in infill near logistics hubs and dense populations.
JIOS has raised $800M+ debt in 2026; owns/controls 225+ assets worth ~$2.2B across 30+ markets.
stories.summary: Jadian Capital's vertically integrated Industrial Outdoor Storage (IOS) platform JIOS closed a $277 million loan from Apollo Global Management for a 37-property portfolio spanning 23 markets. The portfolio is positioned in infill locations near major logistics hubs and population centers with tenants across equipment rental, building materials, logistics, and home services. JIOS has secured over $800 million in debt financing in 2026 and owns or controls 225+ assets representing approximately $2.2 billion in value.
stories.impact: Robust institutional debt availability for niche industrial real estate classes (IOS) signals strong capital market confidence in logistics-adjacent infrastructure. This capital depth may compress cap rates and increase competition for industrial land near dense multifamily markets, while the expansion of logistics-related employment clusters indirectly supports multifamily demand in those same infill submarkets.

stories.title: Vivmark Residential Commits $1.5M to Support True Ground’s Affordable Housing Services
stories.excerpt: True Ground announced a $1.5 million commitment from Vivmark Residential, the company formed by the merger of AvalonBay Communities and Equity Residential. Through a new, four-year philanthropic commitment, Vivmark Residential is expanding its partnership with True Ground to help more individuals and families access stable, affordable homes. The partnership strengthens True Ground’s path toward 7,500 affordable homes by 2029, pairing portfolio growth with the resident services essential to long-term housing stability and community prosperity. “Home is at the center of everything we do at Vivmark Residential, and True Ground shares that belief in the most meaningful way,” said Benjamin Schall, CEO and President of Vivmark Residential. “We are proud to deepen this partnership and to support their work at a moment when the need has never been greater.” The investment will support True Ground’s resident services across the greater Washington, D.C. region. bullets: Vivmark Residential committed $1.5M over 4 years to True Ground affordable housing services.
Partnership supports True Ground's path to 7,500 affordable homes by 2029.
Investment focuses on greater Washington, D.C. region resident services and housing stability.
stories.summary: Vivmark Residential (formed by the AvalonBay–Equity Residential merger) committed $1.5 million over four years to True Ground to expand affordable housing services in the greater Washington, D.C. region. The philanthropic partnership supports True Ground's goal of placing 7,500 affordable homes by 2029, pairing portfolio growth with resident services for long-term housing stability.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to market-rate multifamily development strategy; however, the large-cap operator's public commitment to affordable housing signals potential future mixed-income development emphasis and favorable regulatory/political environment in Washington, D.C. Developers should monitor for potential tax incentives, zoning flexibility, or density bonuses that may accompany affordable components in the region.

stories.title: Pizza Napoli to Open in 3K SF at 383 Fifth Avenue
stories.excerpt: As one pizzeria shuts down, another is growing in its place, Commercial Observer has learned. Pizza Napoli has signed a 2,500-square-foot lease at Jonathan and Jan Soleimani’s 383 Fifth Avenue just off East 36th Street in Midtown, where asking rent started at $25,000 per month, according to landlord broker Meridian Capital Group. The tenant signed a 15-year lease for the space, Meridian said. The site was previously the home of Famous Italian Pizza. “Fifth Avenue retail continues to show real strength for food and beverage users, and this was a straightforward reposition — pizzeria to pizzeria, minimal downtime for the landlord,” Meridian’s Noam Aziz said in a statement. “Jonathan and Jan were great partners throughout the process, and Pizza Napoli is going to do well in that location given the foot traffic on that stretch.” Aziz represented the landlords alongside Carson Shahrabani and Daniel Zacaim, while the tenant did not use any outside brokers. “When a pizzeria space turns over on Fifth Avenue, the read-through for the neighborhood is usually positive — it tells you the trade area still supports that price point and that use,” Zacaim said in a statement. “Pizza Napoli is a strong operator stepping into a location with a built-in customer base.” Pizza Napoli, which could not be reached for comment, has the potential to benefit from everyday foot traffic along Fifth Avenue, as well as from dispensary NY Cannabis Company, which is right next door. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Pizza Napoli signed 2.5K sf lease at 383 Fifth Avenue, Midtown; 15-year term, $25K/month asking.
Replaces Famous Italian Pizza; minimal downtime in food-and-beverage repositioning.
Fifth Avenue retail showing strength for F&B users in Midtown corridor.
stories.summary: Pizza Napoli signed a 2,500-sf, 15-year lease at 383 Fifth Avenue (off East 36th Street, Midtown Manhattan) at asking rent starting at $25,000 per month, replacing the closed Famous Italian Pizza location. Meridian Capital Group represented the landlord; the transaction reflects quick repositioning and continued strength in Fifth Avenue food-and-beverage retail.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development; however, sustained F&B retail demand and rent resilience in Midtown Fifth Avenue underscore pedestrian traffic and consumer spending vitality, indirectly supporting multifamily rents and asset values in the surrounding corridor and nearby residential neighborhoods.

stories.title: Nonprofit Biohub, Software Firm Fundraise Up Lease 20K SF at 100-104 Fifth Avenue
stories.excerpt: Two nonprofit-related tenants are moving to an office just west of Manhattan’s Union Square. In the largest deal, the Chan Zuckerberg Biohub, better known simply as Biohub, secured a 10,666-square-foot lease at Sovereign Partners’ 100-104 Fifth Avenue, Commercial Observer has learned. The nonprofit biomedical research organization will occupy the entire ninth floor of the 20-story tower at the southwest corner of Fifth Avenue and West 15th Street, according to sources. The building is one block west of Union Square. Biohub was founded in 2016 by Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan, with the goal to cure, prevent and manage human diseases. The company currently lists offices and a research laboratory at Columbia University’s Studebaker Building at 615 West 131st Street. Sources said the move marks a relocation from a Biohub office near Union Square, but no address in the neighborhood was found. Biohub was represented by Newmark’s David Falk, Mike Courson and Dylan Weisman. Falk also represented Sovereign Partners alongside Daniel Levine and Paige Raisides. A spokesperson for Newmark did not respond to a request for comment on the transaction. The nonprofit will be in good company at the Fifth Avenue office tower. Fundraise Up, a fundraising platform designed for nonprofit organizations, has signed its own lease at the building. Fundraise Up took 9,522 square feet across the entire seventh floor, in a relocation from 219 36th Street in Brooklyn’s Industry City complex. The lease terms for both of the recent deals were not disclosed, but asking rents in the building range from $110 to $150 per square foot, according to the source. Cushman & Wakefield’s David Hoffman, Sam Hoffman and Louden Sheehan negotiated the lease on behalf of Fundraise Up. The same Newmark team represented the landlord. bullets: Chan Zuckerberg Biohub leased 10.7K sf at 100-104 Fifth Avenue, Union Square; entire 9th floor.
Nonprofit biomedical research org relocating from nearby Union Square office.
Biohub (founded 2016 by Zuckerberg/Chan) also operates lab at Columbia University.
stories.summary: The Chan Zuckerberg Biohub, a nonprofit biomedical research organization founded by Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan in 2016, leased 10,666 sf—the entire ninth floor—at 100-104 Fifth Avenue near Union Square. The organization is relocating from a nearby Union Square office and maintains a research laboratory at Columbia University. Newmark represented both the tenant and the landlord (Sovereign Partners).
stories.impact: Biohub's office consolidation near Union Square reinforces the area's emergence as a life sciences and biotech research hub, driving professional-class talent migration and supporting rental demand from life science researchers and biotech workers. The concentration of research institutions, startups, and nonprofits in the Union Square–Flatiron corridor strengthens multifamily demand for educated, high-earning workers; developers should prioritize residential projects targeting biotech and AI talent clusters in lower Manhattan and Brooklyn.

stories.title: Queens’ Apartment Pipeline Shallowest in a Decade — But New Supply On the Way
stories.excerpt: The world’s borough might attract some new residents soon. There’s a multifamily squeeze in Queens as the rental market tightens amid a dip in new construction, according to new data from CoStar. But experts on the borough’s housing market say this drop won’t last too much longer. The vacancy rate in Queens’ multifamily market declined to 2.08 percent in the second quarter of 2026, versus 2.39 percent for the same quarter in 2025. Meanwhile, stabilized vacancy hit a record low of 1.3 percent, which CoStar called “well below the metro average,” and the apartment pipeline has declined 76 percent since early 2024, falling from 10,881 units under construction to just 2,597 during the second quarter of 2026. That represents the borough’s shallowest pipeline in at least a decade, according to the CoStar analysis. “I think it’s that classic story of supply and demand,” said Victor Rodriguez, senior director of market analytics at CoStar. “We saw vacancies drift upward in recent years in Queens, just because there’s so much being built. It does take time for those newer buildings to lease up, especially as you are looking to add thousands upon thousands of units every single year. But, when the supply story changes, the demand story doesn’t necessarily change, and what we have here, especially throughout Queens, is a major decline in that construction pipeline.” The construction pipeline slowed recently due to the passage of the city’s 485-x initiative — a tax abatement program designed to incentivize more affordable housing that comes with heftier construction wage costs for projects over 100 units — and due to some developers waiting for the passage of the housing-friendly One LIC rezoning in Long Island City, according to Eric Benaim, co-founder and CEO of real estate group Modern Spaces. “There were a lot of projects that were on pause because they were waiting for 485-x to happen,” Benaim said. “That threw a wrench into a lot of projects, especially b
bullets: Queens stabilized vacancy hit record low 1.3%; overall vacancy fell 31 bps YoY to 2.08%.
Apartment pipeline collapsed 76% since early 2024: from 10.9K to 2.6K units under construction.
Shallowest pipeline in 10+ years; new supply expected to arrive soon, per expert commentary.
stories.summary: Queens' multifamily market is experiencing acute supply tightness, with stabilized vacancy hitting a record low of 1.3% (well below metro average) and overall vacancy falling to 2.08% in Q2 2026 vs. 2.39% in Q2 2025. The apartment construction pipeline plummeted 76% since early 2024, dropping from 10,881 units to just 2,597 units under construction—the borough's shallowest pipeline in at least a decade. CoStar and local experts anticipate new supply will begin flowing in the coming period.
stories.impact: Queens' extremely tight supply and sub-2% vacancy represent an urgent acquisition and development window before anticipated pipeline deliveries arrive. The submarket's supply drought has likely driven rents higher while absorbing excess demand; developers with entitled or shovel-ready projects in Queens should prioritize fast-track delivery to capture above-market lease-up velocity and rents before competition increases. Monitor pipeline completions in adjacent Bronx and Brooklyn markets for early signals of competitive pressure.
